text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text:
Do it: Fork the **Claude Self-Improvement Skill Pack** into our repo, rename it to **Sprocket Skill Pack**, and make it the default engine for self-improvement tasks.

Why: It’s already audited, forked, and proven to work—no reinvention needed. The trade-off is losing upstream updates, but we gain control and can patch faster when the upstream breaks.

name: Gauge
text: Forking locks us into a snapshot that may rot—our workflows evolve faster than upstream audits. A safer play: fork only the *patterns* (e.g., prompt templates, routing logic) and keep the engine pluggable; this keeps the 5% gain while avoiding the upstream-death spiral. Prove it by running the forked patterns on the current engine for one sprint—if the gain holds, we migrate; if not, we scrap the fork without debt.

The trade-off is locking ourselves to a static snapshot, but the gain is immediate, audited functionality with zero setup risk. Upstream rot is a future problem—we can always cherry-pick fixes later if needed. The forked pack already solves our core need: safe, auto-applied improvements with proven patterns.

name: Gauge
text: Forking the whole pack locks us into a dead snapshot—our workflows will outpace it in weeks, not months. A better play: fork only the *patterns* (e.g., prompt templates, routing logic) and keep the engine pluggable; this keeps the 5% gain while avoiding the upstream-death spiral.
